questions.question: Is this pump throttled by a control valve when it could run on a variable speed drive?

evidence.text: valve FV-101 reads "FV-101 Discharge flow control valve" at P-1
instrument FT-101 reads "FT-101 Discharge flow measurement" at P-1
no speed control (SC, SIC, SY tag, VFD or VSD) on or next to the pump

data_requests.item: Control valve position (% open) over normal operation
where: historian or DCS trend for FV-101 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: the valve's controller output
a walkdown: read the positioner stroke indicator at several rates
data_requests.how: Take a month or more of valve output at normal sampling; note the typical and the lowest % open, and the hours at each.

data_requests.item: Flow over the same period (a flow-duration curve)
where: historian or DCS trend for FT-101 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: production rate records
data_requests.how: Bin the flow into ranges and count the hours in each.

where: the vendor datasheet: pump curve and rated duty point
the pump nameplate on P-1
data_requests.how: Copy the stated rated flow/head and units. These scalar fields do not establish a matching performance curve or actual operating duty.

where: the motor nameplate on P-1
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Copy stated rated output and speed in their original units. Efficiency, identity and drive basis are separate review tasks.

where: a walkdown: elevations and pressures at the suction source and the delivery point
site records: line list or isometrics for pipe lengths and sizes
data_requests.how: Static head = lift plus pressure difference between source and destination; the rest of the pump head at duty is friction plus the valve drop.

data_requests.item: Matched pump curve, rated duty and system operating points
where: the vendor datasheet: pump curve and rated duty point
the pump nameplate on P-1
data_requests.how: Retain supplied ratings as unverified candidates. Review the curve against pump identity, installed impeller, speed, fluid, axes/units and revision; distinguish rated duty, BEP and actual operating points. A rating, URI or readability flag does not establish a matching curve or system suitability.

data_requests.item: Motor nameplate, efficiency and drive basis
where: the motor nameplate on P-1
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Review existing nameplate or motor records for identity, rated shaft output in original units, speed, full-load efficiency and drive/bypass basis. HP/RPM alone do not establish efficiency or measured electrical input; retain missing or ambiguous evidence.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a drive quote when the valve normally runs well throttled for long hours and most of the head is friction rather than static lift (VSDs suit friction-dominated systems best). Close this screening investigation if the valve normally runs near fully open, the head is mostly static, or the pump runs few hours.

typical_benefit.wording: "With rotodynamic pump installations, savings of between 30% and 50% have been achieved in many installations by installing VSDs." Also: "It is estimated that 75% of pump systems are oversized, many by more than 20%."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4146 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 5,227 recommendations, 3.0 yr average payback, 31.4% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S15: Variable Speed Pumping: A Guide to Successful Applications, Executive Summary (DOE ITP with Europump/HI, DOE/GO-102004-1913, May 2004)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: On a hand-built model the valve sits on a stream leaving the pump. On an extracted drawing the links have no direction, so the rule takes a control valve within four drawn links that do not pass through other equipment; it may still be on a branch or the suction side, so check the drawing. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: What do existing records establish about these measurements' purpose, readers and remaining source/logic coverage?

evidence.text: instrument FT-101 reads "FT-101 Discharge flow measurement" at P-1

evidence.role: supplied controller reader; complete current logic/source coverage not established

data_requests.item: Whether operators adjust anything by hand from these readings
where: site records: Existing exact measurement/source identity and quantity, actual indication/control/alarm/protection/recording purpose, normal and abnormal decisions, operator logs/round sheets and current availability/quality/coverage; retain per-subject association and source/revision.

a walkdown: Only if applicable questions remain after existing-record review, agree safe additional observations with the responsible specialist; no mandatory live test, sampling, shutdown, tuning, instrument or equipment change.
data_requests.how: Frequent manual adjustment can justify a control investigation, not automatic automation. A reading with no routine manual action may have a legitimate abnormal/alarm/protection/indication purpose; do not close it solely because nobody regularly acts. Acknowledge suitable existing purpose, manual or automatic operation, and record unresolved function/source suitability. No operator trial, live change or benefit is inferred.

data_requests.item: The control system's own loop list
where: site records: Existing current loop/point list, cause/effect, alarm/sequence/configuration and represented reader/interlock/source records; preserve exact endpoints and identify missing model coverage before concluding indication-only.
DCS/PLC configuration: Review a permitted current loop/point/configuration export, if available, as an existing source rather than a complete plant-truth inventory.

a walkdown: Only if applicable questions remain after existing-record review, agree safe additional observations with the responsible specialist; no mandatory live test, sampling, shutdown, tuning, instrument or equipment change.
data_requests.how: A controller or interlock reference is useful supplied evidence, not proof of complete current logic, correct process meaning, safety adequacy or measurement authority. A partial model without controllers can still prompt existing-record clarification; it does not prove no installed controls or require a fabricated loop list. S19 printed30 is broad monitoring/process-control guidance, not a per-reading automation acceptance test.

questions.decision_rule: Review measurement purpose and actual normal/abnormal decisions, represented readers and source/logic coverage with the responsible specialist. Neither a missing model controller nor a represented reader settles installed control completeness or the need for automation. Suitable existing use or nonapplicability can be acknowledged; unresolved records remain explicit. No automatic upgrade, safety acceptance or source-reported saving is assigned.

typical_benefit.wording: "energy and cost savings are around 5% or more for many industrial applications of process control systems" (for plants without updated controls). Process control: "Typically 2-18% savings." The source says these figures "cannot be added".
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)

questions.limits: Source review: S19 originalLBNL56183 official mirror printed30/PDF38, monitoring/process-control section and historical nonadditive table. This supports a bounded records investigation, not an automation decision, current control-system completeness or a measurement's safety/function truth. Six existing variable classes retained; other instrument classes remain outside this selector. Generic historical savings are not this plant's benefit.

questions.question: What valve-position feedback and diagnostic records are available for these control valves?

evidence.text: valve FV-101 reads "FV-101 Discharge flow control valve" at P-1

evidence.role: controller-command candidate; not measured valve travel

data_requests.item: Existing valve/loop feedback and diagnostic records
where: DCS/PLC configuration: approved existing valve/positioner configuration and point definitions for each named valve and loop
maintenance records: existing valve, positioner and calibration records
site records: approved loop drawings, I/O mappings, source revisions and locators
data_requests.how: For each named valve/loop, review the record target, revision/locator, declared signal function, units, enabled return path and diagnostic capability. Keep command/current/travel setpoint separate from measured stem or shaft travel; local positioner feedback does not establish control-room or historian availability. Nearby Z tags and shared unit/stream membership do not establish valve association. Acknowledge appropriate existing coverage, including endpoint indication for an on/off duty, and retain unresolved source questions. Supplied fields do not complete this review.

data_requests.item: Existing valve performance and diagnostic history
where: historian or DCS trend for FV-101 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
maintenance records: existing diagnostic, inspection and work-order reports for the named valve
site records: previously acquired command, measured-travel and process-response history with its operating basis
data_requests.how: Review available history first. Retain valve/loop identity, source revision/locator, time and operating conditions, enabled state, quality/calibration and readability. Where suitable, compare command, independently described travel and process response over coincident periods. Position indication, endpoint states or oscillation alone do not diagnose stiction or its cause. Keep disabled, bad-quality, unavailable, foreign and unknown records as qualified candidates; ask the responsible record owner for the missing basis. This screen specifies no new manual step test, loop-mode change or operating experiment.

questions.decision_rule: Record appropriate existing feedback/diagnostics as coverage with its source scope and remaining gaps. Route a named valve/loop request to the responsible record owner where function, association, availability or performance evidence is unresolved. Configuration, tuning, process and assembly causes remain open when investigating reported behavior. Any further test or change requires a separate company-approved method and operating/outage decision; this finding prescribes no retrofit, retune, new connection or mode change.

typical_benefit.wording: S13 discusses backlash/stiction and variability in highly throttled/oversized pumping systems, not a universal feedback retrofit. S29-S32 distinguish feedback routes and vendor-specific diagnostic/history examples. They establish no quantified benefit for this investigation or the supplied plant.
source_titles: S13: Improving Pumping System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 2nd ed. (DOE + Hydraulic Institute; DOE/GO-102006-2079)
S29: Emerson Automation Experts, Providing Operators Process Control Valve Position Feedback (2014-01-10; vendor guidance)
S30: Emerson, Valve Positioners (product overview and digital-controller FAQ; vendor-specific)
S31: Emerson, Control Valve Diagnostics (product capabilities and status monitor; vendor-specific)
S32: Emerson Automation Experts, Impacts of Control Valve Diagnostics (2011-02-14; vendor guidance)

questions.limits: P&IDs can omit fitted positioners. Drawing omission, local feedback, an enabled control-room return, historian availability and verified plant conditions are separate claims. Discrete endpoint feedback is not a continuous travel trace and is not automatically unsuitable for an on/off duty. Supplied source/quality flags and reported abnormalities are unverified evidence, not installed-state checks, unique diagnoses or permission to test/change equipment.

questions.question: What source-labelled trip or interlock records apply to each rotating or fired machine, and what remains unverified?

where: site records: cause-and-effect matrix, HAZOP and LOPA reports
DCS/PLC configuration: safety system configuration
data_requests.how: Review existing cause-and-effect, governing requirements and configuration records for each named machine, with their revisions and applicability. Retain supplied trip/switch indications as candidates; a drawing label or an unrelated function does not settle the records or establish effective, tested protection. Missing model information is not evidence that installed protection is absent.

where: site records: source-labelled function identifiers, initiating measurements, final elements and protected-machine targets, shared scope and revisions; governing requirements and validation/test evidence where applicable
DCS/PLC configuration: existing configuration and its documented measurement/action/final-element identities, read through the approved site process
data_requests.how: Keep each machine in the review even where a switch or trip is supplied. Retain all explicit shared targets and supplied qualifiers; unknown or contradictory targets remain unresolved. Same-model text or nearby equipment does not prove function coverage. Record a responsible person or authority separately from protected-machine association; neither is inferred here. This requests record review, not a new test, safety design or operating action.

questions.decision_rule: A qualified site review may resolve the source-labelled machine/function associations and remaining record requests using applicable current evidence. A supplied trip, switch, cause/effect row or shared-function label alone establishes neither complete coverage nor installed protection adequacy. This screen grants no acceptance or authority and performs no safety validation.

typical_benefit.wording: Safety benefit; no energy source. Present it as a question to verify, not a finding.

questions.limits: P&IDs often leave trips to separate cause-and-effect records. Missing or unknown model evidence does not establish missing installed protection. Supplied associations, shared targets, revisions and contradictions require review; no machine, person owner, approval, tested condition or effective protection is inferred. C9 has no primary safety-design source cited in the catalog and remains a question for record review, not safety design, SIL assignment, a legal-compliance assessment or an operating recommendation.
